title: Stationary-to-weighting moment transfer and spectral rigidity for Boolean Doob kernels
abstract: For positive potentials on a Boolean cube, the stationary density of the noise Doob kernel and its normalized weighting density are different nonlinear functions of the potential. We give an admissible family for which the stationary critical moment is below two while the weighting critical moment is above two, despite a fixed positive stationary floor and exact marginals through order proportional to the square root of the dimension. This refutes transfer of that numerical cap, not the existence of a larger uniform bound. A nonlinear consequence of the stationary floor, combined with classical ordinary and reverse hypercontractivity, gives explicit inverse-potential moments and weighting-moment bounds below a computable finite threshold. Exact stationary matching then gives strong convergence of the two densities throughout this subcritical range. For potentials supported on a binary linear-code Fourier algebra, we control every invariant sector of the full Doob kernel. Under a distance--cardinality condition its gap tends uniformly to the unweighted gap, for every positive quotient potential. Direct disjoint-block estimates cover a sharper parameter regime. A standard simplex code supplies positive potentials outside the disjoint-block class. Classical random linear coding extends this mechanism to positive-rate families at every sufficiently large length, with an explicit exponential gap estimate and normalized witnesses meeting any fixed stationary floor below one and the moment cap. The general stationary-gap question and critical weighting-moment bound remain open.
